$schema-note: The catalogue for --appearance-preset profiles. defaults resolves production appearanceSettingsSchema values through @orb/contracts/settings/appearance; it retains only backgroundLibrary. Other profiles are partial patches over the real getUserSettings response: omitted axes retain account values. Nothing is written. New custom coverage is a profile here, never a CLI flag. Keys and values are validated against the production schema.

defaults.why: Resolved by loadAppearancePreset from appearanceSettingsSchema, not a mirrored patch. Every schema axis resets, including the background selection; backgroundLibrary retains the account uploaded content. Nothing is written.

maximal.why: ALL THE NICE STUFF ON — glow elevation, glass on every surface at a strong radius, grain texture, theme colorization, avatar accent rings, in-chat avatars, and motion actually running. This is the arm a motion/visual audit owes: with the owner's row (reducedMotion on, flat elevation, no texture) every ornament the app ships is invisible to the probe.

compact.why: Minimum chrome at maximum density — compact rows, small square-ish avatars off, no per-message chips, no glass/texture/shadow. The arm where row height, hit targets and truncation defects show up; a comfortable-density pass cannot see them.

reading.why: The long-form reading arm: big type, wide column, document chat style, loosened line height / paragraph spacing / letter spacing, justified body. Every reading-typography var (--reading-*) is off its default here, which is the only way a transcript pass measures them at all.

diagnostics.why: Every per-message diagnostic affordance revealed at once — timer, settled cost, token count, message id, reasoning icon, and the always-expanded action row. These change transcript ROW GEOMETRY (a second metadata line, a permanent action bar), so they are their own layout risk and are OFF in both the schema defaults and the owner's row.
